market.state: UPTREND — CONFIRMED, BUT LEADERSHIP HAS ROTATED OUT OF AI
market.advice: The tape going into the open is genuinely healthy underneath and genuinely nervous on the surface. SPY sits at 776.34, 3.7% above its 50-day at 748.54; breadth is 73% of the scanned universe above its own 50-day; and 142 of 339 rated names register STRONG BUY. That is not a market that is breaking. But VIX at 15.7 is RISING against a 14.9 five-day average, and the reason is on the tape rather than in the charts: Iran has said the Strait of Hormuz stays shut until the US meets its interim-deal conditions, crossings remain in single digits, a vessel was struck by a projectile in the strait overnight, oil is pricing a prolonged crisis, and the 30-year Treasury yield has hit its highest level since 2007. US futures are lower on exactly that. Where the strength actually is matters more than the index: 33 of the STRONG BUYs are financials (BAC, C, JPM, RGA, CFG, MS, USB, PNC, NTRS, MTB all above 89 on single-digit-to-low-teens forward multiples), then healthcare (24), technology (24), industrials (22) and energy (17). Refiners are the cleanest expression of the oil story — MPC at 355.42 and VLO at 341.67 are both sitting within half a percent of 52-week highs having run 20%+ above their 50-days — and they are also the most crowded, because the same headline that fuels them is the tail risk to everything else. Meanwhile the AI complex is still repairing: MU is 19.9% below its high (albeit at 6.5x forward earnings, and TradingView rates it STRONG BUY), AVGO is 18.3% off with TradingView on SELL, AMD 11.5% off, ALAB 33% off, APP 57% off, and AAPL is at RSI 26 — the deepest oversold reading among mega-caps. Plan for the session: normal position sizing, buy the un-extended breakouts in financials, defence, healthcare and datacenter REITs rather than chasing the refiners at the highs, and let the RSI-80-plus names (NTAP 86, MSFT 85, ABNB 82, SCHW 80, SNOW 80, PANW 79) come back to you. Size any energy exposure for the possibility that one de-escalation headline unwinds a week of gains in a single session — and note that rising long-end yields are the one thing that would take the financials trade down with everything else. Utilities and anything bond-proxy remain the weakest group on the board (DTE at RSI 29, KIM at RSI 16).
